content.text:
I added welcome and password reset emails, sent through Resend. Lint is clean. Nothing has been sent or run against Resend. `tsc` reports one error, in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`LayoutProps` not found). That file isn't part of my changes, and I didn't investigate it.

I picked Resend because it has a simple REST API. It's called with plain `fetch`, so there are no new dependencies.

- **`src/lib/email.ts`** (new): `sendEmail`, `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`, each with HTML and plain-text bodies. If `RESEND_API_KEY` or `EMAIL_FROM` is unset, it logs a warning instead of sending, so local dev works.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**: `users.ts` had no way to create a user or reset a password, so I added both.
  - `createUser({ email, name })` normalizes the email, rejects duplicates, and sends the welcome email. A failed send is logged and doesn't fail the signup.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)` creates a random token, stores only its SHA-256 hash with a 60-minute expiry, and emails the reset link. It returns the same result whether or not the email exists, so it doesn't reveal which accounts exist.
  - `consumePasswordResetToken(token)` checks a token once and returns the user it belongs to.
- **`.env.example`** (new): placeholder values for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM` and `APP_URL`. I added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because `.env*` was ignoring it.

Reset tokens live in memory, like the existing user list, so they're lost on restart. Nothing calls these functions yet, and the `/reset-password` page that the email link points to doesn't exist. The app has no password storage, so I didn't build that page or any signup form.
